recipes.name: Tabbouleh
recipes.summary: The Lebanese parsley salad: lots of chopped parsley and mint with a little bulgur, tomatoes, cucumber and lemon.
steps: Pour the boiling water over the bulgur in a small bowl, cover and let stand 20 minutes, until tender. Drain off any extra water and fluff.
Wash and dry the herbs well; wet herbs make a soggy salad. Chop them finely.
Toss the bulgur, parsley, mint, green onions, tomatoes and cucumber with the lemon juice, oil, salt and pepper. Taste and add more lemon if you like.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 2 to 3 days in the fridge. Add the tomatoes the day you serve it so it stays fresh.

freezer.text: Fresh herbs do not freeze well in a salad.

leftovers.text: Tuck leftovers into a pita with hummus.

recipes.kids: Kids can tear the herbs from the stems and squeeze the lemons.

swaps.gluten_free: Use 1 cup cooked quinoa instead of bulgur.

prep_day.ahead: Soak the bulgur and chop the herbs.

recipes.name: Beef and Barley Soup
recipes.summary: Tender beef, pearl barley, mushrooms and vegetables in a rich broth. A cold-weather classic that feeds a crowd.
equipment: large heavy pot or Dutch oven
steps: Pat the beef dry and season with the salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown the beef in 2 batches, 5 minutes per batch. Move to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium. Cook the onion, carrots, celery and mushrooms 8 minutes, until the mushrooms brown. Add the garlic and tomato paste for 1 minute.
Return the beef. Add the broth, thyme and bay leaves, scraping up the browned bits. Bring to a boil, cover and simmer 1 hour.
Stir in the barley and simmer partly covered 35 to 45 minutes, until the beef and barley are tender. Remove the herb stems and bay leaves and stir in the parsley.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge. The barley soaks up broth; add water as you reheat to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze for up to 3 months.

leftovers.text: Pack hot in an insulated food jar for lunch.

recipes.kids: Cut the beef small and serve with a roll for dunking.

swaps.gluten_free: Use brown rice instead of barley (add it for the last 40 minutes) and check the broth.

recipes.name: Mushroom Barley Risotto
recipes.summary: Pearl barley cooked slowly like risotto with browned mushrooms, shallots and Parmesan. Creamy, chewy and filling.
steps: Warm the broth in a small pot and keep it hot over low heat.

Heat 1 tablespoon butter and the oil in a large saucepan over medium-high heat. Cook the mushrooms 8 to 10 minutes, until browned and the liquid is gone. Add the shallots, garlic and thyme and cook 2 minutes.

Stir in the barley for 1 minute. Add 1 cup hot broth and simmer, stirring often, until mostly absorbed. Keep adding broth 1 cup at a time, stirring often, until the barley is tender and creamy, 35 to 40 minutes.
Off the heat, stir in the remaining butter, the Parmesan, salt, pepper and parsley.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge. Reheat to 165°F with a splash of broth.

freezer.text: Freeze for up to 2 months; it will be a little softer.

leftovers.text: Shape cold leftovers into patties and brown them in a skillet.

recipes.kids: Chop the mushrooms small; many kids like them once they are browned.

swaps.gluten_free: Use arborio rice instead of barley; cook about 20 minutes.
swaps.dairy_free: Use oil instead of butter and skip the Parmesan.

prep_day.ahead: Slice the mushrooms and mince the shallots.

recipes.name: Tomato Bulgur Pilaf
recipes.summary: A Turkish-style side of bulgur cooked with onion, pepper and tomato paste. Quicker than rice and full of whole grain.
steps: Heat the oil and butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Cook the onion and pepper 6 minutes, until soft. Stir in the tomato paste for 1 minute.
Add the bulgur and paprika and stir 1 minute. Add the broth and salt and bring to a boil.
Cover, lower the heat and simmer 12 to 15 minutes, until the liquid is absorbed. Take off the heat, lay a towel under the lid and let stand 10 minutes. Fluff with a fork and stir in the parsley.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 5 days in the fridge; reheat to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze for up to 3 months.

leftovers.text: Fold cold leftovers into a salad with chickpeas and cucumbers.

recipes.kids: Serve it like rice; it pairs with almost anything.

prep_day.ahead: Cook a pot for the week.

recipes.name: Mediterranean Quinoa Salad
recipes.summary: Quinoa, chickpeas, cucumber, tomatoes and feta with parsley, mint and a lemon dressing. A meal-prep lunch that keeps for days.
steps: Rinse the quinoa well in a strainer. Bring it and the water to a boil, cover and simmer on low 15 minutes. Let stand 5 minutes, fluff and spread on a plate to cool.
Shake the dressing ingredients in a jar.
Toss the cooled quinoa with the chickpeas, cucumber, tomatoes, onion, feta, parsley, mint and dressing.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge.

freezer.text: Cucumbers and tomatoes do not freeze well.

leftovers.text: Spoon it over greens or into a wrap.

recipes.kids: Serve the feta and vegetables in piles so kids can choose.

swaps.dairy_free: Skip the feta and add olives.

recipes.name: Quinoa Black Bean Salad with Lime
recipes.summary: Quinoa with black beans, corn, red pepper and lots of cilantro in a lime and cumin dressing.
steps: Bring the quinoa and water to a boil, cover and simmer on low 15 minutes. Let stand 5 minutes, fluff and cool.
Whisk the lime juice, oil, cumin, honey and salt in a large bowl.
Add the quinoa, beans, corn, pepper, onion, jalapeño and cilantro and toss.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge.

freezer.text: Best refrigerated.

leftovers.text: Wrap it in a tortilla with cheese, or scoop it up with chips.

recipes.kids: Leave out the jalapeño. Kids like it scooped with tortilla chips.

recipes.name: Turkey and Quinoa Stuffed Peppers
recipes.summary: Bell pepper halves filled with ground turkey, quinoa and marinara, topped with mozzarella and fresh basil.

ingredients.prep: halved through the stem, seeds removed

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Simmer the quinoa covered in the water 15 minutes.

Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the turkey and onion, breaking up the meat, until no pink remains and the turkey reaches 165°F. Add the garlic, Italian seasoning and salt for 30 seconds.
Stir in the quinoa, 1 1/2 cups marinara and the basil. Spread the rest of the sauce in the baking dish, set the peppers in it cut side up and fill them.
Cover with foil and bake 30 minutes. Uncover, top with the mozzarella and bake 10 to 15 minutes, until the peppers are tender and the filling is 165°F.
recipes.make_ahead: Fill the peppers up to 1 day ahead and refrigerate; add 10 minutes to the covered time.

freezer.text: Freeze baked peppers for up to 3 months. Thaw in the fridge and reheat covered to 165°F.

leftovers.text: Chop a leftover pepper into the filling and spoon it over pasta.

recipes.kids: Use a mix of red, yellow and orange peppers and let kids pick a color.

swaps.meatless: Use a can of black beans or white beans instead of the turkey.

recipes.name: Warm Cinnamon Quinoa Breakfast Bowls
recipes.summary: Quinoa simmered in milk with cinnamon and vanilla, like a hot cereal, then topped with berries and a drizzle of maple.
steps: Bring the quinoa, water, milk, cinnamon and salt to a simmer in a saucepan, watching that the milk does not boil over.
Cover and cook on low 15 to 18 minutes, until the quinoa is tender and creamy. Stir in the vanilla and maple syrup.
Spoon into bowls and top with berries and nuts if you like.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge. Reheat portions with a splash of milk.

freezer.text: Freeze cooked portions for up to 2 months.

leftovers.text: Eat it cold with yogurt, like a parfait.

recipes.kids: Kids can add their own toppings from small bowls.

prep_day.ahead: Cook a batch for the week.

recipes.name: Edamame Quinoa Crunch Salad
recipes.summary: Quinoa, edamame, red cabbage, carrots and cilantro in a ginger-sesame dressing. Crunchy and colorful, and it holds up all week.
steps: Bring the quinoa and water to a boil, cover and simmer on low 15 minutes. Let stand 5 minutes, fluff and cool.
Shake the dressing ingredients in a jar.
Toss the quinoa with the edamame, cabbage, carrots, pepper, green onions, cilantro and dressing.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge.

freezer.text: Best refrigerated.

leftovers.text: Add leftover chicken or tofu for a bigger meal.

recipes.kids: Kids can shred the carrots with grown-up help and shake the dressing.

swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari instead of soy sauce.

recipes.name: Moroccan-Spiced Chickpea Stew with Couscous
recipes.summary: Chickpeas, sweet potatoes and carrots in a warmly spiced tomato broth with ginger and cinnamon, spooned over fluffy couscous.
recipes.serving_size: about 1 1/4 cups stew with 2/3 cup couscous
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion 5 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger and spices for 1 minute.
Add the sweet potatoes, carrots, tomatoes, chickpeas, broth, salt and raisins. Bring to a boil, then simmer partly covered 20 to 25 minutes, until the vegetables are tender.
For the couscous, bring the water, butter and salt to a boil. Stir in the couscous, cover, take off the heat and let stand 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
Stir the cilantro into the stew and serve over the couscous.
recipes.make_ahead: The stew keeps 5 days in the fridge; reheat to 165°F. Make couscous fresh; it takes 5 minutes.

freezer.text: Freeze the stew for up to 3 months.

leftovers.text: Serve leftover stew over rice or with warm pita.

recipes.kids: The raisins and sweet potatoes make it a little sweet. Serve it mild with extra couscous.

swaps.gluten_free: Serve over rice or quinoa instead of couscous.
swaps.dairy_free: Use oil instead of butter in the couscous.

recipes.name: Lemon Herb Couscous
recipes.summary: Fluffy couscous with butter, lemon, parsley and mint. Ready in about 10 minutes.
steps: Bring the broth, butter and salt to a boil in a saucepan.
Stir in the couscous, cover, take off the heat and let stand 5 minutes.
Fluff with a fork and stir in the lemon zest, 2 tablespoons lemon juice, parsley, mint and green onions.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge; serve cold as a salad or reheat to 165°F.

freezer.text: Best fresh or refrigerated.

leftovers.text: Toss cold leftovers with chickpeas and cucumber for lunch.

recipes.kids: Kids can zest the lemon with grown-up help.

swaps.dairy_free: Use olive oil instead of butter.

recipes.name: Greek Chicken Couscous Bowls
recipes.summary: Lemon-oregano chicken over couscous with cucumber, tomatoes, red onion, feta and a cool homemade tzatziki.
steps: Toss the chicken with the oil, lemon juice, garlic, oregano, salt and pepper. Refrigerate 30 minutes (or up to 8 hours).
Stir the tzatziki ingredients together and chill.
Bring the water and salt to a boil, stir in the couscous, cover, take off the heat and let stand 5 minutes. Fluff.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken 5 to 6 minutes per side, until it reaches 165°F. Rest 5 minutes and slice.
Build bowls with couscous, chicken, cucumber, tomatoes, onion, feta and a spoon of tzatziki.
recipes.make_ahead: Pack bowls with the tzatziki on the side; they keep 4 days in the fridge. Reheat the chicken and couscous to 165°F or eat cold.

freezer.text: Freeze cooked sliced chicken for up to 3 months; make the bowls fresh.

leftovers.text: Stuff leftover chicken and tzatziki into a pita.

recipes.kids: Kids can build their own bowls; tzatziki makes a good dip for the chicken.

swaps.gluten_free: Use rice or quinoa instead of couscous.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the feta and use a dairy-free yogurt.

prep_day.ahead: Marinate and cook the chicken; make the tzatziki and couscous.

recipes.name: Roasted Vegetable Couscous
recipes.summary: Couscous tossed with roasted zucchini, eggplant, peppers and red onion, a little balsamic and fresh parsley.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the vegetables with the oil, salt and cumin and spread on 2 baking sheets. Roast 25 to 30 minutes, stirring once, until tender and browned at the edges.
Bring the water to a boil, stir in the couscous, cover, take off the heat and let stand 5 minutes. Fluff.
Toss the couscous with the vegetables, vinegar, oil and parsley. Serve warm or at room temperature.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge. Serve cold or reheat to 165°F.

freezer.text: Roasted vegetables turn soft when frozen.

leftovers.text: Add a can of chickpeas and some feta to make it a lunch.

recipes.kids: Cut the vegetables small; roasting makes them sweet.

recipes.name: Salmon with Lemon Dill Couscous
recipes.summary: Salmon baked with lemon and garlic, served on couscous loaded with fresh dill, lemon and peas.
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F and line a baking sheet with parchment. Set the salmon on it, brush with the oil and garlic, season with salt and pepper and top with lemon slices.
Bake 12 to 15 minutes, until the salmon flakes easily and reaches 145°F in the thickest part.
Meanwhile, bring the broth, peas and butter to a boil. Stir in the couscous, cover, take off the heat and let stand 5 minutes. Fluff and stir in the dill and lemon juice.
Serve the salmon over the couscous.
recipes.make_ahead: Make the couscous up to 3 days ahead. Bake the salmon fresh.

freezer.text: Cooked salmon dries out when frozen and reheated.

leftovers.text: Flake cold salmon into the couscous for a lunch salad. Eat within 3 days.

recipes.kids: Kids who are new to fish often like salmon with a squeeze of lemon and a little butter.

swaps.gluten_free: Use quinoa instead of couscous and check the broth.
swaps.dairy_free: Use olive oil instead of butter.

recipes.name: Creamy Tuscan Chicken with Brown Rice
recipes.summary: Browned chicken thighs in a garlicky cream sauce with spinach, roasted red peppers, rosemary, thyme and Parmesan, over brown rice.
recipes.serving_size: 1 1/2 thighs with sauce and 3/4 cup rice
steps: Bring the rice and water to a boil, cover and simmer on low 40 to 45 minutes. Let stand 10 minutes.
Season the chicken with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and brown the chicken 4 minutes per side. Move to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium. Add the garlic, rosemary and thyme for 30 seconds, then the peppers and broth, scraping up the browned bits. Stir in the cream.
Return the chicken, cover and simmer gently 8 to 10 minutes, until it reaches 165°F. Pull out the herb stems.
Stir in the Parmesan and spinach until the spinach wilts and the sauce is creamy. Serve over the rice.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 3 days in the fridge. Reheat gently to 165°F with a splash of broth.

freezer.text: Cream sauces separate when frozen.

leftovers.text: Slice leftover chicken and toss it with the sauce and hot pasta.

recipes.kids: Slice the chicken for kids and serve the sauce over plain rice or pasta.

swaps.dairy_free: Use coconut milk instead of cream and skip the Parmesan.

recipes.name: Wild Rice Pilaf with Cranberries and Pecans
recipes.summary: A holiday-style side of wild and brown rice with shallots, thyme, dried cranberries and toasted pecans.
steps: Bring the wild rice, brown rice, broth and salt to a boil. Cover and simmer on low 45 to 50 minutes, until tender. Let stand 10 minutes, then drain off any extra liquid.
Meanwhile, toast the pecans in a dry skillet over medium heat 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until fragrant. Move them to a plate.
Melt the butter in the skillet. Cook the shallots, celery and thyme 5 minutes, until soft.
Toss the rice with the shallot mixture, cranberries, pecans and parsley.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 5 days in the fridge; add the pecans just before serving so they stay crunchy. Reheat to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze without the pecans for up to 3 months.

leftovers.text: Stir leftovers into a green salad with leftover chicken or turkey.

recipes.kids: Serve the pecans on the side for kids who do not like nuts.

swaps.dairy_free: Use olive oil instead of butter.

recipes.name: Beef Stroganoff
recipes.summary: Strips of sirloin and mushrooms in a creamy sour cream sauce over buttered egg noodles. Comfort food in 45 minutes.

ingredients.prep: trimmed and sliced thin across the grain

steps: Season the beef with salt and pepper. Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet over high heat. Sear the beef in 2 batches, about 1 minute per side, until browned outside and pink inside. Move to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium and add the butter. Cook the shallots and mushrooms 8 minutes, until browned. Add the garlic for 30 seconds, then the flour for 1 minute.

Whisk in the broth, Worcestershire and mustard and simmer 3 to 4 minutes, until thick. Return the beef and its juices and simmer 2 minutes, until the beef reaches 145°F. Let it rest off the heat 3 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook the noodles in boiling salted water by the package directions. Drain and toss with butter.
Stir the sour cream into the sauce off the heat (boiling makes it curdle). Add the parsley and serve over the noodles.

safety.food: beef, pork or lamb steaks, chops and roasts

recipes.make_ahead: The sauce keeps 3 days in the fridge; reheat gently to 165°F without boiling.

freezer.text: Sour cream sauces separate when frozen.

leftovers.text: Spoon leftovers over a baked potato or rice.

recipes.kids: Cut the beef into small pieces; the noodles and creamy sauce win most kids over.

swaps.gluten_free: Use cornstarch instead of flour, gluten-free noodles, and check the Worcestershire label.
swaps.meatless: Skip the beef and use 1 1/2 pounds mushrooms with vegetable broth.

recipes.name: Chicken Paprikash
recipes.summary: The Hungarian favorite: chicken thighs simmered with onions and sweet paprika in a sour cream sauce, served over egg noodles.
recipes.serving_size: 1 1/2 thighs with sauce and 1 cup noodles
steps: Season the chicken with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and brown the chicken 3 minutes per side. Move to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium. Cook the onions and pepper 8 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic, paprika and flour and stir 1 minute; do not let the paprika scorch.
Add the tomatoes and broth and return the chicken. Cover and simmer 20 minutes, until the chicken reaches 165°F.
Meanwhile, cook the noodles in boiling salted water. Drain.
Move the chicken to a plate. Off the heat, stir a little hot sauce into the sour cream, then stir it all into the skillet. Return the chicken, sprinkle with parsley and serve over the noodles.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 3 to 4 days in the fridge. Reheat gently to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze before adding the sour cream for up to 3 months; stir it in after reheating.

leftovers.text: Shred leftover chicken into the sauce and serve over rice.

recipes.kids: Sweet paprika is mild, not spicy. Cut the chicken small for little ones.

swaps.gluten_free: Use cornstarch instead of flour and serve over rice.
swaps.dairy_free: Use 1/2 cup coconut milk instead of sour cream.

prep_day.ahead: Cook the chicken and sauce without the sour cream.

recipes.name: Buttered Parsley Noodles
recipes.summary: Egg noodles tossed with butter, fresh parsley and Parmesan. A simple side kids ask for.
steps: Cook the noodles in a large pot of boiling salted water by the package directions. Save 1/4 cup of the cooking water, then drain.
Return the noodles to the pot with the butter and toss until melted. Add the parsley, Parmesan, pepper and a splash of cooking water and toss until glossy.
recipes.make_ahead: Best fresh. Leftovers keep 3 days in the fridge; reheat with a splash of water.

freezer.text: Best fresh.

leftovers.text: Stir leftovers into chicken soup.

recipes.kids: Kids can sprinkle on the Parmesan.

swaps.dairy_free: Use olive oil and skip the Parmesan.

recipes.name: Tamale Pie
recipes.summary: A chili-style beef and pinto bean filling baked under a golden buttermilk cornbread crust.
equipment: large ovenproof skillet or 9-by-13-inch baking dish
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. In a large ovenproof skillet over medium-high heat, cook the beef, onion and pepper, breaking up the meat, until no pink remains and it reaches 160°F. Drain extra fat.

Stir in the garlic, chili powder, cumin and salt for 30 seconds, then the beans, tomatoes, corn and tomato sauce. Simmer 5 minutes. (Move it to a 9-by-13-inch dish now if your skillet cannot go in the oven.)
Whisk the cornmeal, flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt. Stir in the buttermilk, egg and butter just until mixed, then fold in half the cheese.
Spoon the batter over the hot filling and spread it toward the edges. Sprinkle with the rest of the cheese.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes, until the topping is golden and a toothpick comes out clean. Let stand 5 minutes.
recipes.make_ahead: Make the filling up to 2 days ahead. Reheat it before adding the topping and baking.

freezer.text: Freeze baked portions for up to 3 months. Reheat covered to 165°F.

leftovers.text: Microwave a square for lunch, topped with salsa.

recipes.kids: Kids love the cornbread top. Serve with sour cream and mild salsa.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free flour blend in the topping.
swaps.meatless: Use a second can of beans instead of the beef.

recipes.name: Shrimp and Cheddar Grits
recipes.summary: The Lowcountry favorite: creamy cheddar grits topped with garlicky shrimp, bacon and green onions.
recipes.serving_size: 1 cup grits with about 5 ounces shrimp
steps: Bring the water, milk and salt to a simmer in a saucepan. Slowly whisk in the grits. Cook on low 5 to 7 minutes, whisking often, until thick. Stir in the cheese and butter; cover to keep warm.
Cook the bacon in a skillet over medium heat until crisp, 6 minutes. Lift out and leave 1 tablespoon fat in the pan.

Toss the shrimp with the paprika and pepper. Cook in the hot pan over medium-high heat 2 minutes per side, until pink and opaque all the way through. Add the garlic for 30 seconds, then the lemon juice, most of the green onions, the bacon and hot sauce.
Spoon the grits into bowls, top with the shrimp and sprinkle with the rest of the green onions.
recipes.make_ahead: Peel the shrimp and chop the bacon up to 1 day ahead. The dish is best fresh.

freezer.text: Best fresh.

leftovers.text: Grits firm up in the fridge; reheat with a splash of milk, stirring, to 165°F. Eat leftover shrimp within 3 days.

recipes.kids: Serve the cheesy grits plain with the shrimp on the side.

swaps.dairy_free: Cook the grits in water and broth and skip the cheese and butter.

recipes.name: Creamy Polenta with Garlicky Mushrooms
recipes.summary: Soft, cheesy cornmeal polenta topped with mushrooms browned in butter with garlic and fresh thyme.
steps: Bring the water, milk and salt to a simmer in a heavy saucepan. Slowly whisk in the cornmeal. Lower the heat and cook 20 to 25 minutes, stirring often and scraping the bottom, until thick and creamy. Stir in the Parmesan and butter.

Meanwhile, heat the oil and butter in a skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the mushrooms without stirring for 3 minutes, then stir and cook 5 minutes more, until browned. Add the garlic, thyme, salt and pepper for 1 minute. Stir in the parsley.
Spoon the polenta into bowls and top with the mushrooms.
recipes.make_ahead: The mushrooms keep 3 days in the fridge. Polenta sets as it cools; whisk in hot water or milk to soften it again.

freezer.text: Best fresh.

leftovers.text: Pour leftover polenta into a pan, chill until firm, then slice and brown the pieces in a skillet.

recipes.kids: Polenta is mild and cheesy, a bit like grits. Serve the mushrooms on the side if needed.

swaps.dairy_free: Use water and olive oil and skip the cheese.

recipes.name: Jalapeño Cheddar Skillet Cornbread
recipes.summary: Buttermilk cornbread baked in a hot skillet for crisp edges, with sharp cheddar and a little jalapeño.
steps: Put 1 tablespoon of the butter in the skillet and set it in the oven as it heats to 425°F.

Whisk the cornmeal, flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt. In another bowl whisk the buttermilk, eggs and remaining melted butter. Stir into the dry ingredients just until mixed, then fold in the cheese and jalapeños.
Using oven mitts, take out the hot skillet, swirl the butter and pour in the batter. It should sizzle.
Bake 18 to 22 minutes, until golden and a toothpick comes out clean. Cool 10 minutes before slicing.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 2 days at room temperature wrapped well, or 5 days in the fridge.

freezer.text: Freeze wedges wrapped well for up to 3 months.

leftovers.text: Crumble leftovers over chili, or toast a wedge with butter for breakfast.

recipes.kids: Leave the jalapeños out of half the batter for a mild side. Grown-ups handle the hot skillet.
